newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ING Barings modifies EPS on some Hungarian shares.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings modifies EPS on some Hungarian shares.

text.p: In the September issue of its "Eastern European Monthly" ING Barings modified its earnings/share (EPS) forecasts for several Budapest-traded shares and in some cases it revised its recommendations, too.
ING Barings revised its EPS estimate for pharmaceuticals maker Egis upwards to 774 forints from 727 for 1996 and its EPS forecast to 997 forints from 945 for 1997.
It attributed the change to "favourable change in product mix, better-than-expected control over R&D spending, improving margins." ING Barings left its rating unchanged at "buy".
The securities house raised its 1996 EPS estimate to 246 forints from 195 and to 409 forints from 376 for 1997 for brewery Sopron and revised its rating to "long-term buy" from "hold."
Sopron's positive assessment reflected the beneficial impact of the launch of its joint distribution network with Martfu Brewery at the beginning of this year.

The Budapest bourse's only foreign issue, packaging firm Cofinec, was dowgraded to "hold" from "buy" and its EPS forecast was reduced to 175 forints from 435 for 1996 and to 445 forints from 664 for 1997, after it released disappointing first half results.
ING Barings left its recommendations unchanged for retailer Fotex, hotelier Danubius and oil company MOL, but the forecasts were reduced.

The EPS estimate for Fotex which was left as "reduce" was lowered to 12 forints from 16 for 1996 and to 16 forints from 22 for 1997, on "difficult market conditions and internal restructuring underway."
Danubius, a "long-term buy", was reduced to an EPS of 206 forints from 219 for 1996 and is forecast to have an EPS of 272 forints from 303 in 1997.
ING Barings explained this by the hotelier's financing needs of its recent acquisitions of Hungaria hotel chain.
MOL's EPS was reduced after the Hungarian government decided to postpone the energy price increase to January 1, 1997 from October 1, a step which will chop off MOL's profits this year.

The oil company is estimated to have an EPS of 107 forints, down from 125 in 1996 and 180 forints, compared to the earlier forecast of 183 forints in 1997. MOL's recommendation remained "long-term buy."
